Tara (Customer): Hey team — customer reports SDK token estimator is ~4.2k but the Redwood invoice shows 5.8k for the same session. Can someone help reconcile? :confused:
Maya (Support): Thanks for flagging — can you paste the request payload (messages array) and the SDK version used? Any screenshots of the usage dashboard vs invoice help.
Tara (Customer): Using redwood-js v0.8.1. Payload (redacted):
```json
{"model":"redwood-2o","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are a helpful assistant."},{"role":"user","content":"Summarize the following docs..."},{"role":"assistant","content":"(tool call)invoke_pdf_parser"},{"role":"tool","name":"pdf_parser","content":"<extracted text 32KB>"},{"role":"assistant","content":"Here is the summary..."}],"max_tokens":512}
```
Tara (Customer): SDK's client.tokensEstimate() returns 4201. Invoice shows 5789 tokens for the same session id. Dashboard usage line for the model shows 5.7k tokens.
Maya (Support): Got it. First-pass: system & role separators, function/tool messages, and how the server reserializes tool responses can add tokens. Also billing counts the full serialized request + any server metadata.
Jason (Eng): Quick checklist we usually run: 1) Which tokenizer/version used by client estimate? (tiktoken compatibility matters). 2) Are you including tool outputs in the estimator or only user+assistant? 3) Any trailing hidden metadata (e.g., trace IDs) included on the server?
Sam (SDK): SDK v0.8.1 uses the local lightweight estimator that mirrors GPT-style tokenization but it intentionally omits role delimiter tokens by default to avoid overcounting for devs. That causes underestimates for sessions with many function/tool messages.
Tara (Customer): Ah — so SDK omits role separators? That's surprising. Can you show the repro snippet we should use to match billing numbers?
Sam (SDK): Repro snippet that matches server tokenization:
```js
const payload = {model:'redwood-2o', messages: [...]};
// use the full server tokenizer helper
const est = await client.internalTokenize(payload, {includeRoleSeparators:true, includeToolOutputs:true});
console.log(est.tokens);
```
Maya (Support): Also note server-side we canonicalize function/tool messages into a single assistant message: we append the function name and JSON payload which can add tokens (and braces). That explains ~15-35% bumps depending on tool size.
Jason (Eng): Short technical explanation for the billing team: our metering pipeline tokenizes the canonicalized payload that we persist for audit. That includes the system message, explicit role strings, function call name, and full tool outputs. Client-side quick estimators skip some of that for perf.
Tara (Customer): Is there any quick math to decide whether invoice is wrong vs expected? Customer says delta ~38%.
Oliver (Billing Bot): If delta > 20% we escalate to billing audit. Please attach: request_id, session_id, and server-side logs for the session window (we can fetch trace if you give root request_ts).
Maya (Support): Action items: (1) Tara, send the request_id + the session timestamp. (2) Tara, run the internalTokenize snippet Sam provided to compare. (3) Jason, can you confirm whether any server pre-processing adds hidden tokens (e.g., newline after system)?
Jason (Eng): Confirmed: we add "\n\n" separators and a role prefix for each message like "system:" "user:" "assistant:" before tokenization — that's 2-6 tokens per message on short messages.
Tara (Customer): Sharing request_id: r-8a3f2c, ts: 1775551200. Running the internalTokenize now...
Sam (SDK): FYI: we can add a flag in SDK v0.8.2 to surface the server-style estimate by default (`serverStyleTokenEstimate: true`) if this pattern is common.
Maya (Support): Temporary workaround: instruct customers to include tool outputs in their estimator or set a safety multiplier (1.2) when reporting estimated usage for billing-sensitive apps.
Jason (Eng): For engineering follow-up: we should document exactly what the metering tokenizer includes (role prefixes, separators, function-call wrappers). I'll open an eng-doc and link here.
Maya (Support): Tara — Billing team will run an audit using request_id. Expect update in 24-48h. For the immediate ask: if the customer needs a credit, escalate after audit if we confirm meter overcount (rare) or provide a credit if misbilling found.
Tara (Customer): Thanks — I'll provide logs and let the customer know the workaround. Appreciate quick triage. :pray:
Oliver (Billing Bot): Audit queued: audit-177555-8a3f2c. Billing will update thread when complete. :mag:
